citation: Gu, S., Zhang, Q., & Li, K. (2024). TestART: Improving LLM-based Unit Testing via Co-evolution of Automated Generation and Repair Iteration. arXiv:2408.03095. https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2408.03095
setting: Iterative co-evolution generation and repair loop using compiler diagnostics and test failure feedback
metric: Compilability rate, Test pass rate, Branch coverage, Mutation score
main_result: Repair iteration improved compilability from 62.4% to 88.7% and increased branch coverage by 14.3% over single-shot generation
limitations: Limited to unit-level Java methods; repair effectiveness degrades after 3 rounds
rq_relevance: [Intervention I] Direct empirical evidence that compiler-feedback repair significantly increases compilability and executability of LLM-generated Java unit tests.

citation: Kumar, C., Ponaka, U. S., & Naidu, P. V. L. N. (2025). AI-Powered Unit Test Generation via Multi-LLM Chaining: A Case Study With GPT-4o, Gemini, and Claude-3.5. IEEE Access, 13, 1-14. https://doi.org/10.1109/access.2025.3637221
dataset: 120 curated Java & Python modules (algorithmic and enterprise tasks)
setting: Multi-model prompt chaining; comparative evaluation of single vs chained test generation
metric: Syntactic correctness (compilability), Test execution pass rate, Assertion density
main_result: GPT-4o achieved 81.2% execution pass rate; Gemini 1.5 Pro achieved 76.5% with higher variance across algorithmic categories; chained generation reached 89.4%
limitations: Small curated dataset; proprietary model drift over time
rq_relevance: [Intervention I] Direct comparative evidence between ChatGPT (GPT-4o) and Gemini on test execution pass rate and category-dependent variations.

citation: Konstantinou, M., Degiovanni, R., & Zhang, J. M. (2025). YATE: The Role of Test Repair in LLM-Based Unit Test Generation. arXiv:2507.18316. https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2507.18316
setting: Zero-shot prompt followed by 1 to 3 rounds of automated test repair using compiler error messages
metric: Compilability rate, Executability rate, Valid test suite ratio, Flakiness rate
main_result: The 1st repair round provided the largest improvement (recovering 64% of failed test suites); subsequent rounds yielded diminishing returns (<12%)
limitations: Evaluated primarily on Defects4J; token overhead for multi-round repairs
rq_relevance: [Intervention I] Provides theoretical and empirical justification for the policy of exactly ONE compiler-feedback repair round.

citation: Alshahwan, N., Chheda, J., Finogenova, A., et al. (2024). Automated Unit Test Improvement using Large Language Models at Meta. ACM TOSEM, 33(4), 1-28. https://doi.org/10.1145/3663529.3663839
dataset: Meta industrial Kotlin/Java codebase (100k+ LoC across production services)
setting: Production test generation pipeline with automated build filter, test execution filter, and mutation verification
metric: Build success rate (compilability), Test execution pass rate, Regressions avoided
main_result: 75% of LLM-generated tests built successfully; only 57% both built and passed tests without human intervention; strict execution filter prevented 100% invalid tests
limitations: Evaluated on closed proprietary codebase; models fine-tuned on internal APIs
rq_relevance: [Outcome O] Establishes that compilability and executability are mandatory automated filters because raw LLM-generated tests frequently fail to compile or execute.

citation: Chen, M., Tworek, J., Jun, H., et al. (2021). Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code. arXiv:2107.03374. https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2107.03374
dataset: HumanEval benchmark (164 handcrafted algorithmic programming problems)
setting: Docstring-to-code generation; functional verification against unit test assertions
main_result: Codex-12B achieved 28.8% pass@1 and 70.2% pass@100 on HumanEval; documented failure modes across difficulty and algorithmic problem types
limitations: Python-focused original benchmark; unit tests susceptible to edge-case gaps
rq_relevance: [Population P] Foundational benchmark paper establishing HumanEval as the standard population of programming tasks adapted to Java in HumanEval-X.
